description: This archived dataset from the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics, part of the National Transportation Atlas Database, is the National Petroleum Council petroleum liquids transportation network of 1995 for crude oil and petroleum products. It is a straight-line origin-to-destination network, not mapped pipeline routes. The archive, documented in a README dated 4 June 2025, holds two shapefiles of links and nodes, one for the crude oil network and one for the petroleum products network, a text file with methodology and a data dictionary, a data management plan and DCAT-US JSON metadata. The data are in the public domain and are available to download free through the DOT ROSA P repository under a DOI, with a recommended citation. Coverage is the United States in 1995. Caveats: the network is thirty years old and schematic, so it suits historical or topological studies, not current routing, and the ROSA P landing page refused automated reading, so details come from the README. Simulation uses are a simple national petroleum pipeline graph for network flow and supply chain disruption experiments. Related records: data-eia-us-energy-atlas-and-maps and data-npms-national-pipeline-mapping-system cover current pipelines.
